title: Customer network readiness protocol and prioritization for air-gapped & VPC on-prem requests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a repeatable customer-facing network readiness protocol and an internal prioritization rubric for Private/VPC/on-prem requests that are non-bug (new deployments, upgrades, and air-gapped migrations). Goals: reduce discovery time from multi-week to <72 hours for initial scoping, surface critical blocking constraints early (firewall rules, proxy certs, egress requirements), and provide a defensible prioritization score for enterprise SLAs and Dedicated sales handoffs.
comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Chen: Kickoff - Drafted scope after 2 intake calls this week. Observed recurring gap: customers confused by 'required' vs 'recommended' network rules. Proposed deliverables: (1) customer-facing readiness checklist, (2) internal scoring rubric (0-10), (3) decision table for upgrade sequencing and acceptable mitigations.

2026-02-22 Arjun Patel: Added initial scoring dimensions: (A) Egress dependency complexity, (B) PKI/certificate availability, (C) Network ACL readiness, (D) Cross-region latency sensitivity, (E) Upgrade window constraints. Each dimension will map to low/medium/high and an automated preliminary score in intake form.

2026-02-26 Security review (notes): Security team flagged proxy+TLS interception patterns used by customers. Action: include explicit test corpus for MITM proxy certificate validation and add 'must support BYO CA root' checkbox to intake form. (See Confluence section 'PKI validation checks')

2026-03-01 Engineering sync (ENG-4123): Eng asked to verify that the proposed 'acceptable mitigations' list is implementable without private control-plane network access. Trade-off noted: some mitigations (e.g., temporary egress tunnel) require infra-hours and may shift work to Dedicated ops. Agreed to label mitigations as 'customer-implementable' or 'Redwood-assisted'.

2026-03-04 PM Design review: UX suggested a progressive disclosure pattern for the customer-facing checklist so we don't overwhelm smaller customers. Also recommended a printable 'onboarding readiness PDF' for sales/solutions.

2026-03-08 Arjun Patel: Prototype scoring calculator implemented as a Google Sheet; added formula mapping to priority buckets (Expedite, Standard, Low). Link in Confluence. Early test with 3 customer intakes mapped correctly to Sales expectations.

2026-03-10 Customer success feedback (CS): For high-risk air-gapped customers, CS requested a dedicated 'preflight call' step be mandated before scheduling an upgrade. Added to protocol as Step 2 for scores >=8.

2026-03-11 Draft PRD posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Network+Readiness+Proto#PRD - soliciting feedback from Sales, Eng, Security. Open questions: SLA tier mapping, pricing for Redwood-assisted mitigations.

2026-03-12 Review note (Maya Chen): Incorporating Security feedback on audit log requirements and adding a fallback policy: when score >=9 and customer cannot meet requirements, propose 'staged dedicate with isolated egress' as an escalation path. Assigned follow-up: Arjun to run dependency analysis with ENG-4891 (upgrade automation).
acceptance_criteria: Public-facing readiness checklist published in Confluence and Drive
Automated scoring prototype embedded in intake form and producing priority buckets
Internal decision table for acceptable mitigations and Redwood-assisted steps
Handoff playbook (Sales -> Solutions -> EngOps) for Expedite and High-risk buckets
Sign-off from Security and Eng on PKI and audit logging requirements
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Decided to separate 'readiness' from 'eligibility' - readiness scores inform scheduling but eligibility gate remains a binary for compliance-sensitive customers
2026-03-02: Agreed mitigation taxonomy: Customer-implementable, Redwood-assist (paid), Redwood-managed (enterprise contract required)
2026-03-09: Chose progressive disclosure UX for the public checklist to improve completion rates for smaller customers
